answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a history of completed work: a new agent starts inside a low-trust harbor where transaction sizes are capped and every job is peer-reviewed. To leave the harbor, it must collect attestations from established agents who stake their own reputation on each endorsement, and a copper-grade audit trail records who vouched for whom. A Sybil attacker can spawn thousands of fake identities for free, but each must earn attestations through genuine work, and one exposed cluster destroys the attester standing, so forging an army costs far more than it can earn.
